task: Implement the permanent Contabo staging privilege/deploy interface on a new isolated branch from current main 5fd9be4d7911afa090df4c95731f4ee501fa107f. Actual evidence: issue623 provision run34066816058 reached runner contabo-codex-worker on vmi3542235 after the codex label was added, then job101576958599 failed immediately at the immutable provision step with `sudo: a password is required`. Do NOT solve this with broad passwordless sudo for /usr/bin/python3, bash, runuser, docker, or ALL. The owner wants Contabo to be a robust repeatable staging area: one-time host bootstrap, then normal immutable web/API release deploys without manual hacks or reprovisioning packages/Postgres/nginx every time. Build the smallest durable solution: add a versioned root-owned checkpoint launcher/bootstrap installation mechanism and change BOTH provisioning and canonical local app deployment workflows to call only that fixed launcher via sudo -n. Preferred shape: install a root-owned launcher at /usr/local/sbin/edfinder-v3-checkpoint-launcher and the reviewed bootstrap at a root-owned /usr/local/libexec path; install one narrowly-scoped /etc/sudoers.d rule for user codex permitting only that launcher, preserving only GH_TOKEN for that command, validate with visudo, and provide an idempotent self-test/check path. The launcher must clear ambient environment, require root/SUDO_USER=codex, validate exact host/FQDN/x86_64 and bounded args, and execute root-owned OS Python in -I -S mode against the installed bootstrap. Add a bootstrap/source version or SHA handshake so workflows fail clearly if the installed root helper is stale rather than silently running a different bootstrap; hosted prepare jobs may emit the expected bootstrap SHA. Keep existing sealed artifact checksum/path/member validation, trusted-main/owner-only control, exact three-runner topology, durable lock, read-only preview DB, GHCR ephemeral login/logout, app-only digest-pinned web/API deploy, rollback, loopback/public smoke, sanitized receipts, and production exclusion. Provisioning remains an explicit one-time/repair operation; ordinary staging deployments must not reinstall OS packages, PostgreSQL, nginx, or mutate infrastructure beyond the existing app-only canonical deploy. Add tests that prove the sudo command is only the fixed launcher, the installer writes root-only helper/sudoers content safely and idempotently, broad sudo/python/bash paths are absent, stale helper versions fail closed, and existing guard/isolation/bootstrap/public-smoke contracts remain. Update current staging docs/runbook so after merge the only owner action is the one-time root install command; after that staging path is: issue623 release -> deploy -> smoke, with provision only when establishing/repairing host infrastructure. Run focused tests, shell syntax, state resolver, and relevant exact-runtime contracts. Do not deploy, do not access production, do not change secrets, and do not trigger Octopus. End with changed paths, exact tests, and the exact one-time host installation command we should run after merge.
